newsitem.title: FRANCE: SIA to add two weekly Paris-Singapore freighters.
newsitem.headline: SIA to add two weekly Paris-Singapore freighters.

text.p: Singapore Airlines (SIA) said it planned to introduce two, additional weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter flights between Paris/CDG to Singapore, in conjunction with Air France, effective end-March 1997, instead of one as initially planned.

"The two additional frequencies will take the weekly number of joint SIA/Air France freighter flights on the route to five," David Lim, SIA's London-based regional cargo manager, Europe, told Reuters.
He added: "We had already decided on a fourth weekly freighter flight having operated it on an adhoc basis last Autumn and at the beginning of this week agreed to operate a fifth."
With the introduction of the fifth frequency, SIA is to drop its weekly 747-200F service between Basle and Singapore, Lim said.
"Freight normally carried by this service will be flown out on SIA's service from Paris or Frankfurt and we will be maintaining our sales office in Basle."
The upgrade of the Paris-Singapore service was down to the buoyant level of outbound and inbound traffic and strong demand forecasts for 1997, he added.
Of the five weekly Paris-Singapore 747-200 freighter frequencies, operating next March 30, Air France aircraft will operate three and SIA two.
"With four of the five frequencies, capacity will be shared on a 50/50 basis but on the fifth, space will be shared around 70/30 in Air France's favour."
From June 1 1997, SIA plans to replace its two 200Fs on the route with 400F "Mega Arks" which offer 10 to 20 tonnes extra caapcity per flight as a result of an extra main deck position.
SIA also carries freight on a daily, non-stop Airbus 340-300E passenger service between Paris and Singapore.
The aircraft can accommodate around 11 tonnes of cargo per flight on the route.

1996 air cargo exports on the Paris-Singapore route totalled 9,054 tonnes, an increase of 20.5 percent on 1995, Paris airport authority figures showed. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
